title: Human Resources Officer
experience_raw: Senior (5+ years of experience)
raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE (TORs) FOR RECRUITING HUMAN RESOURCE OFFICER FOR FAWE RWANDA CHAPTER 1. Background The Forum for African Women Educationalists (FAWE) is a membership-based Pan-African Non-Governmental Organization that operates through 34 National Chapters in 33 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa to promote girls’ and women’s education. FAWE’s vision, mission and goal focus on quality education for girls and women socio-economic empowerment. FAWE Rwanda is one of 33 national chapters. FAWE Rwanda Chapter was started in 1997 and since its inception, FAWE Rwanda has grown to become a reputable partner and focal point on female education in Rwanda. FAWE Rwanda Chapter would like to recruit a Human Resource Officer for an initial period of three years, renewable based on performance and availability of Funds, with a probationary period of three months. Details of the position are provided below: Position: Human Resources OfficerReports to: Executive Director 2. Job Purpose The core purpose of the Human Resources Officer is to support the Executive Director in the effective management and administration of the organization’s human resources. The position is responsible for supporting staff recruitment and onboarding, maintaining personnel records, coordinating staff performance management and capacity-building initiatives, administering staff welfare and benefits, and ensuring compliance with FAWE Rwanda’s human resources policies, procedures, and applicable employment regulations. The Human Resources Officer will also promote gender-responsive, equitable, and inclusive human resource practices aligned with FAWE Rwanda's mission of advancing girls' and women's education and empowerment, while championing organizational values, staff wellbeing, safeguarding, and professional excellence. 3. Key Responsibilities Serve as the focal point for the Human Resources function within the organization and provide timely HR support to management and staff. Support workforce planning and ensure the effective implementation, interpretation, and continuous improvement of HR policies, procedures, systems, and practices. Support strategic workforce planning, succession planning, and talent management initiatives to ensure the organization attracts, develops, and retains high-performing employees. Coordinate end-to-end recruitment and selection processes, including developing job descriptions, preparing vacancy announcements, shortlisting candidates, coordinating interviews, conducting reference checks, facilitating onboarding, and ensuring timely updates of employee information in the ERP system. Maintain accurate, complete, and confidential employee records, including personnel files, staff databases, employment contracts, leave records, attendance records, and other HR documentation, ensuring that relevant information is properly maintained in the ERP system. Coordinate the staff performance management process in collaboration with Department Heads, including performance planning, objective setting, performance appraisals, feedback, and follow-up on performance improvement and development plans. Support employee engagement and welfare initiatives, address workplace concerns appropriately, and promote a positive, respectful, inclusive, and productive working environment. Coordinate staff wellbeing initiatives and promote a healthy work environment through wellness programs, psychosocial support initiatives, and work-life balance practices. Work with management to identify staff capacity-building and professional development needs and coordinate relevant training, staff orientation, coaching, mentoring, and other learning and development initiatives. Develop and implement annual staff learning and development plans to strengthen organizational capacity and support career growth. Collaborate with the Finance and Administration Department to provide accurate and timely HR information for payroll processing and ensure the effective administration of employee benefits in accordance with organizational policies, with relevant transactions and records maintained through the ERP system. Monitor and administer staff attendance, leave, and other absences, ensuring compliance with approved policies and procedures and maintaining accurate records through the ERP system. Ensure compliance with applicable HR policies, procedures, and employment legislation, including FAWE Rwanda policies and relevant labor laws and regulations in Rwanda. Coordinate the implementation of safeguarding, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), anti-harassment, and child protection policies, ensuring staff awareness and compliance with organizational standards. Prepare and submit regular HR reports to the Executive Director and provide management with accurate and timely HR information on staffing levels, recruitment, turnover, leave, attendance, performance, training, employee welfare, and other relevant HR matters. Analyse workforce data and HR trends, including staff turnover, recruitment efficiency, retention, training effectiveness, and employee engagement, to support evidence-based management decisions. Facilitate effective HR communication by communicating HR policies, procedures, benefits, and organizational decisions to staff and providing appropriate guidance and clarification on HR-related matters. Coordinate employee lifecycle processes, including induction, probation monitoring, confirmation, promotion, transfer, resignation, termination, exit interviews, clearance, and separation procedures. Provide HR advisory support to management and employees on HR policies, employee relations, performance management, and other employment-related matters, while supporting the fair, consistent, and confidential resolution of workplace issues. Identify and monitor HR-related risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures to ensure organizational effectiveness and compliance. Ensure confidentiality and proper management of employee data by safeguarding personnel information, maintaining secure HR records, and ensuring that access to confidential employee information is restricted to authorized personnel in accordance with organizational policies and applicable data protection requirements. 4. Reporting and Working Relationships The Human Resources Officer will report to the Executive Director or designated supervisor and will work closely with programme, finance, administration, and other departments to ensure effective human resource management across the organization. 5. Qualifications and Experience A bachelor’s degree in human resources management, Business Administration (Specialization in Human Resource Management), or a related field with at least 5 years of relevant experience in human resources management, preferably within an NGO or similar organization. or A master’s degree in human resources management, Business Administration (Specialization in Human Resource Management), or a related field with at least 2 years of relevant experience in human resources management, preferably within an NGO or similar organization. Professional certification in Human Resources Management is an added advantage. Training or certification in safeguarding, child protection, gender equality, diversity and inclusion, or organizational development will be an added advantage. Good knowledge of employment practices, HR policies, and applicable labor laws in Rwanda. Experience in recruitment, talent management, performance management, employee relations, learning and development, safeguarding compliance, and HR administration. Strong communication, interpersonal, organizational, and problem-solving skills. Good computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office and HR information systems. High level of integrity, confidentiality, professionalism, and attention to detail. 6. Key Competencies The Candidates should have the following key competencies: Human resource management and administration, Recruitment and talent management, Employee relations, Performance management, Training and capacity development, Strategic workforce planning, Leadership and people management, Coaching and mentoring, Organizational development, HR analytics and data-driven decision-making, Gender-responsive human resource management, Diversity, equity and inclusion, Safeguarding and child protection, Change management, Risk management and compliance. Communication and interpersonal skills, Planning and organizational skills, Conflict management and problem-solving, Confidentiality and integrity, Teamwork and collaboration. Commitment to girls' education, women's empowerment, gender equality, and safeguarding principles. 7. Key Deliverables The Human Resources Officer will be expected to deliver: Accurate and up-to-date personnel records and HR databases (ERP-Microsoft Dynamics 365). Timely and well-coordinated recruitment and onboarding processes. Effective implementation of staff performance management processes. Regular HR reports submitted to management. Effective administration of staff leaves, benefits, and welfare. Coordinated staff training and capacity-building activities. Compliance with HR policies and applicable employment regulations. A professional, supportive, and productive working environment. Annual staff learning and development plan implemented. Quarterly HR workforce analytics reports submitted to management. Staff well-being and engagement initiatives effectively coordinated. Safeguarding and PSEA compliance measures implemented and monitored. Updated succession planning and talent management records maintained. Gender-responsive and inclusive HR practices promoted across the organization. 8. Duration and Terms of Employment The appointment will be for an initial period of three years, renewable based on performance and availability of Funds with a probationary period of 3 months) 9. Remuneration and Benefits FAWE Rwanda Chapter offers a competitive remuneration package commensurate with the successful candidate’s qualifications, skills, and relevant professional experience. The benefits package includes medical insurance, pension contributions, maternity leave, airtime allowance, and annual leave, in accordance with FAWE Rwanda’s policies and applicable employment regulations 10. Job application procedures Application letter addressed to FAWE Rwanda National Coordinator and Education certificates (combined in pdf); Recent Curriculum Vitae (CV) with proven work Experience including three referees (combined in pdf). Highly qualified candidates should send their cover letter; well detailed CV and copies of degrees and certificates. How to Apply Interested candidate should submit their application no later than 15th October 2026. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply

raw_text: Description Position Title: Biobank Head Department: Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER) Duty Station: UGHE-AVEGA Biobank and UGHE, Kigali. Frequent travel to the Butaro campus, Northern Province, Burera District, Rwanda Contract Duration: Two (2) years, renewable based on performance Position Summary The Biobank Head provides strategic, scientific, technical, and operational leadership for the establishment and management of the UGHE-AVEGA Biobank, a core research infrastructure of the Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER). The position is responsible for leading the planning, establishment, operationalization, accreditation, and continuous improvement of the biobank to support clinical trials, translational research, precision medicine, genomics, oncology, infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, and population health research. The Head is responsible for the overall administration and day-to-day management of biobank operations, including biospecimen acquisition, processing, storage, inventory management, retrieval, distribution, Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) administration, quality management systems, biosafety and biosecurity, regulatory compliance, equipment management, financial oversight, and supervision of biobank personnel. Reporting to the Clinical research lead/Director of IGHER, the Biobank Head works closely with the Head of the UGHE-AVEGA Clinical Trial Unit to ensure seamless integration of biobanking services into all clinical trials and research activities conducted through UGHE. The position also collaborates closely with the Biobank Project Consultant (External Scientific Consultant) to establish the biobank according to international standards, develop governance structures, implement quality systems, strengthen institutional capacity, and position UGHE as a national and regional centre of excellence in biobanking. The Biobank Head will play a pivotal leadership role in developing institutional policies, standard operating procedures, governance frameworks, regulatory systems, quality assurance programs, and strategic partnerships that ensure the biobank operates in accordance with ISBER Best Practices, ISO 20387, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and all applicable national and international regulatory requirements. Key Responsibilities Lead the establishment and operation of the UGHE–AVEGA Biobank and align activities with UGHE/IGHER priorities. Establish SOPs, Quality Management Systems, governance, and regulatory compliance, including preparation for ISO 20387 accreditation and ISBER Best Practices. Lead implementation and management of the LIMS and ensure secure, accurate, and traceable data management. Oversee biospecimen management, quality, traceability, security, staffing, equipment, budgets, and daily operations. Integrate biobanking with clinical trials and research programs and develop national and international collaborations. Build staff capacity through training, mentorship, and competency development in biobanking, GCP/GCLP, biosafety, and quality management. Qualifications Education PhD (preferred) or Master's in Biobanking, Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biomedical/Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Pathology, Genomics, Public Health, Clinical Research, or related field. Certification in GCLP, GCP, ISO 20387, ISO 15189, ISBER Best Practices, or QMS/Laboratory Management is a plus. Experience 8+ years in biobank management, biomedical research, clinical laboratory management, or clinical trial support, including 5+ years in senior leadership supervising multidisciplinary teams Proven track record establishing or expanding a biobank/biospecimen repository — infrastructure planning, workflow development, and operations Experience implementing LIMS and laboratory/biobank Quality Management Systems Hands-on management of biospecimen collection, processing, cryopreservation, storage, and distribution Equipment lifecycle management (procurement through calibration/maintenance) Experience managing donor-funded programs, budgets, and strategic/donor reporting Developed SOPs, quality manuals, and governance structures (Oversight/Scientific Advisory/Data Access Committees) Prepared labs for ISO 20387, ISO 15189, or ISBER accreditation; built CAPA and audit systems Prepared IRB/ethics/regulatory documentation; ensured compliance with biospecimen collection, storage, and export regulations Developed informed consent, data privacy, and biobank governance frameworks Supported regulatory inspections and audits Strong command of ISBER, ISO 20387/15189, GCLP/GCP, LIMS, and biosafety/QMS standards. Excellent leadership, project and financial management, and scientific writing/communication skills. Experience establishing a national/regional biobank; integrating biobanking into clinical trials; working with international institutions or in LMIC/Africa settings; PMP/PRINCE2 certification; strong publication and grant-management record. To apply Applicants should provide: (1) a curriculum vitae, (2) graduate transcripts, (3) examples of relevant teaching experience or course materials, where available, and (4) a personal statement describing their teaching approach and experience working with diverse student populations. Applicants may also include an example of relevant scholarly work. Please upload these under the ‘Additional Files’ tab on the application page. University of Global Health Equity is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Organizational Profile UGHE is a new kind of university focused on training the next generation of global leaders in health care delivery. The university launched in Rwanda in September 2015. Through an academic experience uniquely rooted in the values of equity, students are empowered to both ease suffering at the bedside and drive transformational, systemic changes to the health system. UGHE is an initiative of Partners In Health (PIH), an internationally recognized non-profit organization whose mission is to provide a preferential option for the poor in health care. In over nearly three decades of operating alongside public sectors in countries around the world, PIH has developed a model to deliver high quality healthcare to some of the world’s most marginalized communities. Nowhere has this impact been more profound than in Rwanda, where Inshuti Mu Buzima-PIH’s sister organization and our government partners have driven innovation for a decade. Members of the UGHE community are tenacious and resolute in our drive to attain social justice, make common cause with those in need, listen to and learn from others, and operate with honesty and humility as we uphold academic integrity and intellectual curiosity. The University of Global Health Equity seeks individuals committed to these values to join the team. Commitment to Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Sexual Harassment: At UGHE, we are committed to ensuring that those who benefit from our work- including community members – as well as our students, contractors, staff, and visitors to our campus are treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment and any form of systemic abuse, whilst reducing risk and vulnerabilities. A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with UGHE’s policy. UGHE will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of fraud, harassment, sexual harassment and any form of systemic abuse or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By applying, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures. Apply

TerraFund focuses on deploying grants, low-interest loans, and equity finance to organizations in three key landscapes: the Lake Kivu & Rusizi River Basin (in Burundi, DRC, and Rwanda), the Greater Rift Valley of Kenya, and the Ghana Cocoa Belt. These portfolios are managed through the World Resources Institute’s TerraMatch platform, an end-to-end system that hosts open calls for proposals, connects champions with technical assistance, and tracks the progress of funded projects through a standard monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) protocol. With this data, VIA Foundation is building new partnerships that catalyze finance for restoration outcomes. Internship Highlight: VIA Foundation seeks a Communications Intern to help tell the story of locally led restoration across Africa. Working from the Kigali office, you will help build the foundation’s young public voice producing content for its website and LinkedIn, capturing stories from the restoration champions it finances, and assembling the communications materials that support its partnerships and fundraising. This is a hands-on learning role designed for a recent university graduate who writes well, is curious about restoration and climate finance, and wants to build a professional portfolio. You will be expected to draft, design, publish materials, and take ownership of the pieces assigned to you. You will report to the Grants & Finance Specialist and work closely with VIA Foundation’s Project Managers, its Field Coordinators in Rwanda, Kenya, and Ghana, and communications colleagues at VIA Foundation’s technical partner WRI Africa. Over six months, you will see how an emerging pan-African institution positions itself with funders, governments, and the communities restoring degraded land. Key Responsibilities: Content Creation (50%) Draft and edit short-form content champion profiles, field stories, blog posts, newsletter copy, event recaps, and captions in clear, accessible English. Work with Project Managers and Field Coordinators to gather photographs, quotes, and stories from restoration sites and nurseries through both the TerraMatch platform and turn them into publishable material. Build simple visual assets — social graphics, slide templates, one-pagers, and carousels — using Canva or similar tools, in line with VIA Foundation’s brand guidelines. Maintain an organized library of photos, videos, logos, consent forms, and approved messaging so that materials can be reused quickly and correctly. Support the drafting of communications products that strengthen fundraising and donor engagement, such as impact snapshots, portfolio highlights, and annual report sections. Support the preparation of materials for external forums where VIA Foundation is represented. Digital Channel Management (50%) Maintain and update content on via-foundation.org, including news items, partner pages, and vacancy postings. Prepare, schedule, and publish posts across VIA Foundation’s LinkedIn and monitor comments and messages for follow-up. Build a mailing list of VIA Foundation’s partners through which to share news and updates. Maintain the communications calendar, tracking upcoming publications, events, campaign moments, and portfolio milestones. Compile monthly analytics on website traffic and social media performance, and flag what is working and what is not. What you will learn: How a financial intermediary communicates restoration finance to funders, governments, and local organizations. Practical digital communications skills: content management systems, social publishing and analytics tools, and basic design and multimedia editing. How to mine online reporting systems to tell stories from the field. A portfolio of published work — written pieces, visual assets, and campaign materials — that you can carry into your next role. What you will need: Education: A completed bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, international development, environmental studies, or a related field. Recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Experience: Up to 2 years of experience — including internships, student media, volunteer work, or freelance assignments — in communications, content creation, or digital media. Excellent written English, with a demonstrated ability to turn complex or technical material into clear, engaging copy. A portfolio, writing samples, or links to published work are required. Familiarity with major social media platforms and how organizations use them, including basic content planning and audience engagement. Working knowledge of design and editing tools such as Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or CapCut; comfort with photography or short-form video is an advantage. Basic experience with website content management, e.g., Drupal, and with social media or web analytics is an advantage. Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage several assignments against deadlines in a small, fast-moving team. Demonstrated interest in ecosystem restoration, climate, agriculture, or sustainable development. Comfort receiving and acting on editorial feedback across multiple rounds of revision. Languages: You will be proficient in written and spoken English and fluent in Kinyarwanda. Additional fluency in French and/or Swahili is an asset. Requirements: You must have an existing right to work in Rwanda and be able to work in person from VIA Foundation’s Kigali office. Travel: Willingness to travel occasionally to restoration sites in Rwanda to gather stories and content. Internship Terms: This is a full-time, six-month paid internship based in Kigali, Rwanda. The intern will receive a monthly stipend in RWF. The intern will receive regular supervision, feedback, and mentoring, and will have access to learning opportunities across VIA Foundation and its partner network. How to apply? A 1-page cover letter specifying why you are an excellent fit for the internship. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture. Programs Overview The Government of Rwanda (GoR) strives to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by enabling equitable access to quality health services for the population as outlined in the Fourth Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP IV). This commitment has been made against a backdrop of rising health care costs and uncertainty around the future availability of donor funding and calls for improved health sector sustainability. Acknowledging this, the Government aims to employ effective, equitable, efficient, and sustainable health care financing and systems strengthening, putting an emphasis on primary health care as the cornerstone of a strong and sustainable health system. CHAI Rwanda’s Health System Strengthening (HSS) programs work on a day-to-day basis with Government leadership in the Ministry of Health (MoH) and the Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB). The goal of those programs is to support the Government to accelerate progress towards UHC by ensuring the sustainable delivery of quality, essential health services. This includes designing and implementing national Primary Health Care (PHC) reforms from health center level down to community health, to increase health workforce availability, to prioritize and sustainably finance essential services, and to support improved management, financing, and delivery of quality primary health care. The role ensures that health data is transformed into high-quality, reliable, explainable, and decision-ready intelligence that informs AI development, policy decisions, and health system performance improvement. This role serves as the technical bridge between raw health data, AI models, and real-world decision-making, ensuring scientific rigor, reproducibility, and national-scale usability. Health Systems Intelligence & Decision Support Develop decision-support analytics and public health dashboards for disease burden tracking, resource allocation and service delivery optimization. Support training and continuous professional development of healthcare providers on study interventions and data reporting requirements. Contribute to the analysis and interpretation of maternal and neonatal health data to inform implementation improvements. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Medicine and Surgery, Nursing, Midwifery, Public Health, or a related field. Proven experience in maternal health projects, research, or clinical program implementation. Strong familiarity with Rwanda’s health system, Ministry of Health structures, and national data reporting mechanisms. Demonstrated experience mentoring and supporting healthcare providers in data quality, clinical documentation, and protocol adherence. Experience coordinating field-based health sector activities. Excellent analytical, organizational, and documentation skills with high attention to detail. Effective communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills to engage multidisciplinary teams. Strong commitment to ethical research practices, patient confidentiality, and professional integrity. Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and travel frequently to field sites. Why Join This Project? Contribute directly to improving the quality of maternal and neonatal health services in Rwanda. Play a key role in strengthening clinical practice and implementation research at facility level. Work closely with national health authorities and multidisciplinary teams on high-impact interventions. Support evidence-based improvements that influence national health policy and practice. Job Purpose: The Plant Manager leads the day-to-day running of Kivu Choice’s fish processing plant, ensuring that machinery-heavy production lines run safely, efficiently, and without unplanned stoppages. The role owns process control, preventive and corrective maintenance, and quality and food safety compliance across the plant, while leading shift teams and operators. As Kivu Choice scales volumes toward 30,000 tons a year, this position is critical to protecting throughput, yield, and product quality from intake through to cold storage and dispatch. Key Responsibilities: 1. Production & Process Control Plan and run daily production to meet volume, yield, and quality targets across all processing lines. Set, monitor, and adjust process parameters (line speeds, temperatures, and processing times) to keep output consistent. Develop and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) for every line and piece of equipment. Identify bottlenecks and lead continuous improvement to raise throughput and reduce waste. Coordinate with harvest, logistics, and sales teams so that raw material intake matches plant capacity and orders. 2. Preventive & Corrective Maintenance Build and run a preventive maintenance schedule for all plant machinery, refrigeration, and utilities. Lead fast troubleshooting and corrective repairs to keep unplanned downtime to a minimum. Maintain equipment history, maintenance logs, and a critical spare parts inventory. Manage external technicians and suppliers for specialized servicing and repairs. Advise on equipment upgrades, new installations, and capacity expansion. 3. Quality Control & Food Safety Implement and maintain food safety systems in line with HACCP, GMP, and ISO 22000 principles. Monitor critical control points and ensure corrective action is taken and documented when limits are breached. Enforce hygiene, sanitation, and cleaning-in-place standards across the plant. Prepare the plant for internal, customer, and regulatory audits (e.g. Rwanda FDA, RSB) and close out findings. Ensure full product traceability from raw material intake to finished goods. 4. Cold Chain & Product Integrity Oversee chilling, freezing, and cold storage operations to keep product within required temperature ranges. Monitor and record temperatures across processing, storage, and loading points. Work with logistics to protect cold chain integrity through dispatch and distribution. 5. Shift Leadership & People Management Lead, schedule, and supervise shift supervisors, machine operators, and line workers. Enforce occupational health and safety standards and lead incident investigations. 6. Production Reporting & KPIs Track and report daily, weekly, and monthly KPIs, including throughput, downtime, yield, and waste. Analyze performance trends and present root causes and action plans to management. Maintain accurate production, maintenance, and quality records. Support budgeting for plant operations, maintenance, and spare parts. Qualifications & Experience: Bachelor’s degree or advanced diploma in mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, industrial, or food process engineering, food science, or a related field. At least 5 years of experience in a processing plant (food, beverage, dairy, meat, poultry, or fish processing preferred), including hands-on supervision of machinery-heavy production lines. Strong process control skills and proven experience running preventive and corrective maintenance programs. Working knowledge of quality control and food safety standards such as HACCP, GMP, or ISO 22000. Cold chain or perishable-product experience is a strong plus. Proven ability to lead shift teams and operators in a production environment. Comfortable with production reporting and KPIs such as throughput, downtime, and yield; good working knowledge of Excel. Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose equipment and process issues quickly under pressure. Rwandan national, or already holding the right to work in Rwanda (Kivu Choice is not able to sponsor work permits for this role). Fluency in English and Kinyarwanda; French or Swahili is an advantage. raw_text: Job Description: General Practitioner (GP) Department/Unit: Ketamine Treatment & Research Center (KTRC)Duty Station: King Faisal Hospital Rwanda, KigaliReports to: Designated KTRC Clinical Lead / Head of DepartmentEmployment Terms: 1 year renewable Position Overview The General Practitioner (GP) will provide medical assessment, monitoring, and follow-up care for patients receiving ketamine-assisted treatment at the Ketamine Treatment & Research Center (KTRC). Working closely with psychiatrists, nurses, psychologists, and other healthcare professionals, the GP will identify and manage medical risks, respond to adverse events, and ensure safe, coordinated patient care in accordance with approved clinical protocols, hospital policies, and applicable professional and regulatory standards. Key Responsibilities Conduct medical histories and physical examinations, review medications and comorbidities, identify contraindications and drug interactions, and request appropriate investigations or specialist assessments. Assess patients' medical status before treatment and communicate relevant findings and recommendations to the treating psychiatrist and multidisciplinary team. Monitor patients during treatment sessions in collaboration with the nursing team and respond to medical complications within professional competence. Recognize clinical deterioration, adverse reactions, and emergencies, initiate appropriate interventions, and activate hospital emergency pathways when necessary. Assess medical stability and discharge readiness, provide post-treatment precautions, and coordinate referrals and follow-up care. Participate in multidisciplinary case discussions and collaborate with the clinical team to ensure continuity and quality of care. Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential clinical records, including assessments, monitoring observations, interventions, and adverse events. Contribute to clinical audits, quality improvement, safety protocol reviews, and approved research activities in accordance with ethics approvals and confidentiality requirements. Comply with hospital policies, infection prevention standards, medication safety requirements, professional ethics, and continuing professional development requirements. Authority and Accountability The GP shall perform medical assessments, monitoring, interventions, and follow-up within the limits of professional registration, demonstrated competence, hospital privileges, and approved KTRC protocols. The GP's responsibilities include: Medical assessment and monitoring: Identifying medical risks, assessing patient stability, and supporting safe treatment delivery. Emergency management: Providing initial medical care, recognizing complications, and escalating cases requiring specialist intervention. Patient follow-up: Providing discharge advice, coordinating referrals, and supporting continuity of care. Documentation and quality improvement: Maintaining clinical records and contributing to audits, incident reporting, and approved research activities. Multidisciplinary collaboration: Communicating effectively with the treating psychiatrist and other healthcare professionals. Psychiatric diagnosis, psychiatric risk assessment, complex psychotropic medication decisions, and psychiatric treatment planning remain the responsibility of the treating psychiatrist. The GP shall not independently initiate or modify ketamine treatment outside approved protocols and the established authorization framework. Decisions regarding treatment eligibility, continuation, postponement, or discontinuation shall follow the designated clinical decision-making process. raw_text: Regional Human Rights Specialist, Africa Rwanda Full-Time GLOBAL CONSERVATION Job Description Reports To: Director, Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU) Location: Kigali, Rwanda (or another WCS Africa hub location) Country Program/Sector: APAMU /Africa Program Position Type: Full-time Scope/Capacity: Africa-wide Coordinates with: APAMU Team, Rights & Communities, Rights & Communities Regional and National Staff, Regional Leadership Teams, Country Directors, Landscape Leads, Protected Area Managers, Law Enforcement Advisors, Program Development Teams, and Technical Working Groups About Us The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is a private, nonprofit U.S. organization founded in 1895. Its mission is to preserve wildlife and wild places by understanding critical issues, developing science-based solutions, and taking conservation action that benefits nature and humanity. With more than a century of experience, long-term commitments in dozens of landscapes, a presence in more than 60 countries, and experience creating more than 150 protected areas worldwide, WCS has accumulated the biological knowledge, cultural understanding, and partnerships necessary to ensure that wildlife and wild places thrive alongside local communities. WCS recognizes that nature and people are intrinsically linked, and that biological and cultural diversity are interdependent, mutually reinforcing and often co-evolved. Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities frequently represent the most active defenders of nature, and we believe that respecting and protecting the rights of Indigenous Peoples and local communities reflects our global commitment to equity and justice and is our best pathway to achieving durable conservation. About the Africa Program WCS manages one of the largest conservation portfolios in Africa, supporting protected and conserved areas, community-led conservation, key biodiversity landscapes, species conservation initiatives, and wildlife law enforcement efforts across multiple countries. Globally, WCS also supports Indigenous and Traditional Territories, a growing opportunity to center guardians of nature and to secure their rights. The Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU) seeks to ensure that conservation outcomes are achieved in a manner that applies WCS policies, principles and commitments. The Global Rights and Communities (R&C) unit provides guidance and tools across WCS countries to promote community conservation, ensure social safeguards and promote respect for human rights and positive relationships with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and other rights holders. This position will play an important role in coordinating and contributing to a standardized approach to human rights protection in Africa, with the guidance of APAMU, Global R&C and close collaboration with regional and country teams. Job Purpose The Regional Human Rights Specialist will lead and support the standardization of human rights integration and rights-based approaches across WCS conservation programs throughout Africa. The position will provide strategic and technical guidance to country programs and field sites to support human rights integration in conservation law enforcement, conduct human rights impact analyses, assist in investigation or fact-finding around human rights issues as requested, develop recommendations for country programs or landscapes to address human rights issues and risks, and oversee the review of rights-respecting Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for field operations. This position reports to the Director of Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU), and will play a critical role in the APAMU team in fulfilling the needs of a human rights based approach. The position will maintain a dotted line of reporting to the Senior Human Rights Specialist in Rights & Communities Global, for final approval and review of substantive human rights products and in order to coordinate with broader WCS policy and approaches outside of Africa. The position will also coordinate closely with regional and country level human rights, law enforcement, safeguards and communities staff. This position will require significant travel to remote field locations and sites where WCS works, and working with diverse teams from different country programs. The candidate will be expected to undertake planning and coordination as necessary with global, regional and country or site-level counterparts. Major Responsibilities 1. Human Rights Strategy and Integration Work with Senior Human Rights Specialist to ensure the implementation of WCS's rights-based conservation approach across all Africa programs. Coordinate with Regional Social Safeguards leads to support country programs and landscapes to integrate human rights into conservation planning, project design, budgets, monitoring, and reporting. Provide technical guidance on international human rights standards applicable to conservation programming. Promote alignment between WCS sites, country and regional level management, APAMU, and Rights & Communities. Support the development and review of organizational guidance, tools, frameworks, and operational procedures related to human rights. 2. Human Rights Impact Analysis and Risk Management Conduct human rights impact assessments and analyses for new sites and other situations as needed. Identify actual and potential human rights risks associated with conservation interventions and recommend practical mitigation and management measures. Contribute to the development and maintenance of systems for tracking human rights risks, corrective actions, lessons learned, and emerging trends across Africa programs. 3. Human Rights and Conservation Law Enforcement Work closely with the APAMU Law Enforcement Strategist and Senior Human Rights Specialist to provide strategic guidance on the integration of human rights principles into conservation law enforcement operations. Support law enforcement teams, site managers, and country programs to ensure that internationally recognized human rights standards are observed, and protocols are adequate for monitoring, and training. Support the development, review, and implementation of rights-respecting law enforcement policies, protocols, and operational guidance. 4. Development of Rights-Respecting SOPs Review Africa-level Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that embed human rights principles into field operations as needed together with regional safeguards leads, based on WCS institutional policies. 5. Training and capacity building Design and deliver human rights trainings with a focus on practical application of human rights protection and human rights-based approaches in the context of field implementation, community conservation and conservation law enforcement (or equivalent) 6. Other tasks as needed Review protocols and process relating to mainstreaming of gender equity, respect for the rights of Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and underrepresented groups in program design and management. Contribute technical content for donor reports and organizational reporting related to human rights commitments and achievements. Qualification Requirements Advanced degree in Law or other relevant field with a specialization in human rights; a first degree with relevant experience and certificates can be accepted in lieu of an advanced degree. Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in human rights advocacy, research, policy or monitoring and reporting. Proven experience working directly with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, civil society organizations, and/or government stakeholders in the context of Africa. Fluency in English and ability to work professionally in French. Desirable Qualifications Experience in conservation programs or issues relating to conservation. Experience with grassroots advocacy or human rights defenders. Fluency in Portuguese or African languages relevant to program areas. Core Competencies and Skills Technical Competencies Strong knowledge of international human rights standards and frameworks, and regional African frameworks Knowledge of both civil law and common law based systems for law enforcement. Understanding of human rights-based approaches to conservation and development including institutional due diligence practices. Demonstrated experience conducting human rights assessments and risk assessments and to develop appropriate methodologies. Understanding of gender integration, Indigenous Peoples rights. Experience developing policies, guidance documents, and operational procedures. Professional Skills Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills. Effective at organization, time-management, and self-directed field work. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills. Strong stakeholder engagement and interview skills. Ability to work effectively across cultures and multidisciplinary teams. Ability to influence and support change across diverse country programs. raw_text: Description Job Title: Civil & Structural Technician Department: Infrastructure Duty Station: UGHE, Butaro, Rwanda Reports To: Civil and Structure Engineering Manager Employment Type: Full-time 1. JOB PURPOSE The Civil & Structural Technician will provide practical technical and maintenance support for the University's civil infrastructure, buildings, and external facilities. The position will be responsible for routine inspection, preventive maintenance, minor civil repairs, building-fabric works, site measurements, workmanship checks, defect reporting, and support to approved facilities improvement projects. The successful candidate should be a hands-on, multi-skilled technician capable of working independently on routine tasks while also supporting contractors, artisans, engineers and facilities staff. The position requires good practical knowledge of civil works, basic structural elements, building maintenance, drainage, paving, and general building fabric repairs. The technician will be expected to identify defects and unsafe conditions, carry out authorized remedial works, maintain accurate work records, and promptly escalate major structural, safety or specialist issues to the responsible supervisor. 2. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES A. Civil Infrastructure Inspection and Maintenance Inspect assigned external civil infrastructure and building elements on a routine basis. Inspect and maintain paths, paving, steps, surface drains, gullies, and minor boundary works. Identify and report on settlement, cracking, blocked drainage, trip hazards, erosion and other defects. Identify potential concerns affecting retaining structures or other structural elements and escalate them appropriately. Carry out authorized minor repairs and maintenance works. Clear authorized drainage blockages and maintain serviceable access routes. Coordinate with gardening and other maintenance staff where vegetation affects drainage, access or civil infrastructure. Maintain accurate inspection and maintenance records. B. Building Fabric and Minor Civil Works Execute approved minor civil and building fabric maintenance works. Undertake practical repairs involving finishes, doors, roofs, drainage and other related building elements where safe and within assigned competence. Prepare work areas, tools, equipment, and materials before commencing assigned tasks. Take measurements and quantities required for maintenance and repair work. Carry out minor masonry, plastering, concrete, paving, drainage and related repair activities. Inspect completed works for workmanship and identify defects requiring correction. Complete assigned snagging and remedial work. Maintain clean, safe, and organized work areas. C. Facilities Improvement and Project Support Support approved civil components of facilities improvement projects. Assist with site measurements, setting out, access arrangements and preparation of materials. Provide practical site support to engineers, project managers, and contractors. Monitor assigned works and provide observations on workmanship, materials, and defects. Assist with snag identification and closure. Support civil interfaces associated with projects such as drainage, water infrastructure, tanks, STP works, grey-water systems, fire-protection infrastructure and other facilities improvements as assigned. Maintain records of site observations, measurements, completed works, and outstanding items. Work within approved drawings, specifications, scope, and instructions. D. Contractor and Workmanship Support Support the Facilities/Infrastructure team in monitoring contractor activities within assigned areas. Verify dimensions, quantities and completed works where assigned. Observe workmanship and report defects or deviations from approved requirements. Assist in preparing areas for contractor activities and coordinating access. Participate in inspections and snagging exercises. Provide evidence of completed works and support project close-out documentation. Escalate major technical, structural or specialist works to the responsible engineer/manager. E. Tools, Materials and Work Planning Prepare required tools, equipment, and materials for assigned work. Ensure appropriate tools are used safely and correctly. Report shortages, damaged equipment, or unsuitable materials. Assist with material measurements and usage records. Maintain tools and equipment in good working conditions. Keep work areas clean and properly protected during maintenance activities. F. Health, Safety, Quality and Environmental Compliance Comply with all applicable workplace health and safety requirements. Conduct pre-work checks and identify hazards before commencing activities. Use appropriate PPE and safe working methods. Follow safe procedures for working at height, manual handling, dust-producing activities, access works and use of tools/equipment. Protect building users, staff, visitors and property while carrying out maintenance work. Maintain good housekeeping at all work locations. Promptly report hazards, incidents, near misses and unsafe conditions. Stop and escalate work where conditions exceed the technician's competence or authorization. Maintain required quality and maintenance documentation. G. Documentation and Reporting Maintain complete work orders and maintenance records. Record inspections, defects, measurements, materials used and completed works. Provide photographic or other evidence of completed works where required. Record and follow up on outstanding defects and snags. Provide regular updates to the supervisor responsible. Ensure assigned work orders are properly closed out. Maintain accurate records of safety observations, incidents, and near misses. 3. KEY DELIVERABLES The Civil & Structural Technician will be expected to deliver: Safe and serviceable external civil infrastructure. Timely completion of assigned minor civil and building maintenance works. Accurate inspection and defect records. Properly completed and documented work orders. Effective identification and escalation of structural and major civil defects. Quality workmanship on authorized in-house repairs. Effective support to contractors and facilities improvement projects. Timely closure of assigned snags and defects. Proper material and tool utilization. Compliance with health, safety, and quality requirements. 4. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE Minimum Qualifications Advanced Diploma in Civil Engineering, Civil Engineering Technology, Building Technology, Construction Technology or related technical field. A recognized technical/vocational qualification in civil construction or building works may also be considered supported by relevant practical experience. Experience • Minimum 2–3 years of relevant practical experience in civil works, building maintenance, construction or facilities maintenance. • Practical experience in the maintenance of buildings and external infrastructure is highly desirable. • Experience working with contractors and multidisciplinary maintenance teams is an advantage. • Experience in an institutional, commercial, healthcare, educational, or similar environment is desirable. 5. TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES The candidate should demonstrate practical competence in: General civil construction and maintenance. Concrete and minor reinforced concrete works. Masonry and plastering. Paving and external work. Surface drainage and gullies. Minor building repairs and building fabric maintenance. Basic understanding of structural elements and common structural defects. Basic site measurement and quantity take-off. Reading and interpreting basic construction drawings. Basic setting out and levels. Identification and reporting of construction defects. Basic use and care for construction tools and equipment. Workmanship inspection and snagging. Basic maintenance documentation and reporting. Occupational health and safety procedures. 6. HANDS-ON / MULTI-SKILLED REQUIREMENT The successful candidate should be willing and able to perform practical hands-on duties rather than functioning solely in an office or supervisory capacity. The technician should be capable of assisting with or performing, within their competence and authorization: Minor masonry repairs. Concrete repairs. Plastering and patching. Paving repairs. Drainage cleaning and minor repairs. Kerb and walkway repairs. Minor boundary wall repairs. Door and building fabric repairs. Minor roof-related maintenance support. Painting and surface preparation. Basic carpentry-related building maintenance. General facilities repair and maintenance activities. Preparation of work areas and materials. Site housekeeping and protection. Where a task requires specialist engineering design, structural assessment, major construction, electrical/mechanical expertise or other specialist competence, the technician must escalate the matter to the responsible professional or contractor. 7. BEHAVIOURAL AND PERSONAL COMPETENCIES The successful candidate should demonstrate: Strong practical and hands-on attitude. Reliability and punctuality. Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Good attention to detail. Strong safety awareness. Good problem-solving ability. Ability to identify and report defects accurately. Good communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to follow instructions, drawings, and technical requirements. Good work discipline and housekeeping. Ability to prioritize maintenance tasks. Professional conduct when working around staff, students, patients, visitors, and contractors. Willingness to learn and undertake different facilities-related tasks within the technician's competence. 8. REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS The Civil & Structural Technician will report to the Civil and Structure Engineering Manager and will work closely with: Civil/Structural Engineers. Facilities and maintenance personnel. MEP technicians. Project managers. Contractors and artisans. Procurement and stores personnel. Security and other relevant institutional departments. 9. AUTHORITY AND LIMITS OF RESPONSIBILITY The technician is authorized to undertake approved routine maintenance and minor civil works within their demonstrated competence. The technician shall not independently approve, design or execute major structural works or specialist works outside their competence. Structural defects, major cracks, significant settlement, major drainage failures, structural instability, major alterations and other high-risk or specialist works shall be promptly reported and escalated to the responsible engineer/manager. Major works and specialist contractor activities remain subject to the University's approved project management, engineering and procurement processes. 10. PERFORMANCE INDICATORS Performance will be assessed against: Completion of assigned maintenance work orders within agreed timelines. Quality and durability of completed repairs. Accuracy and completeness of inspection and maintenance records. Timely identification and escalation of defects and safety risks. Effective closure of assigned snags. Compliance with approved drawings, instructions, and work methods. Compliance with health and safety requirements. Proper use of tools, materials, and equipment. Effective support for projects and contractors. Good housekeeping and protection of institutional facilities. Combine similar requests where possible to obtain better prices and reduce the number of orders. Sourcing and Quotations Follow the procurement method set out in the company's Procurement Manual for every purchase, and obtain the quotations or bids that the method requires. Identify and maintain a list of reliable, approved suppliers for all goods, materials, equipment and services needed by the company. Compare the quotations or bids received on price, quality, delivery time and payment terms, and prepare the comparison for approval as required by the Procurement Manual. Negotiate prices and terms with suppliers in the best interest of the company, within the limits of the Procurement Manual. Confirm that the selected supplier is registered and can issue a valid EBM invoice. Purchase Orders Prepare and issue a PO to the selected supplier only after the purchase has been approved. State on every PO the item description, quantity, unit, agreed price, delivery date and delivery place. Record every PO in the Excel PO register, showing PO number, supplier, items, amount, order date, expected delivery date and status. Follow up with suppliers to make sure goods are delivered on the agreed date, and inform the requesting department and the store of any delay. Delivery, Invoices and Payment Support Work with the Store Keepers and the Equipment Store Officer to make sure every delivery is physically counted and matched against the PO, the supplier delivery note and the EBM invoice, and that the price agrees before the invoice is passed for payment. Resolve shortages, damaged goods, wrong items and price differences with suppliers, and arrange returns, replacements or credit notes. Hand over the complete set of documents (PO, delivery note and EBM invoice) to the Equipment Store Officer for receiving in QBO, and to Finance for payment. Supplier Management Evaluate supplier performance regularly on quality, delivery time, price and service. Handle any claim about the quality of goods supplied directly with the supplier, supported by the Store Keeper's and the user department's records. Keep supplier contracts, agreements and contact details up to date and filed. Report poor or unreliable suppliers to the Procurement Section Leader, with a recommendation on whether to continue buying from them. Records and Reporting Keep all procurement documents (requests, quotations, comparisons, POs, delivery notes, EBM invoices) filed in order and available for audit. Prepare a weekly and monthly procurement report showing purchases made, pending orders, late deliveries and cost savings. Ethics and General Responsibilities Act with honesty and integrity, and avoid any conflict of interest in dealing with suppliers. Do not accept gifts, favours or payments from suppliers or potential suppliers. Follow company procurement policies and procedures, and the applicable laws and tax requirements. Perform any other related duties assigned by the Procurement Section Leader. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Economics or a related field [2-3] years of relevant procurement experience, preferably in mining, construction, or another heavy industry Professional certification (e.g., CIPS) is an added advantage Solid knowledge of procurement procedures, contract management, and tendering processes Familiarity with mining equipment and supply chains is an added advantage Strong negotiation, analytical, and communication skills What We Offer Competitive salary commensurate with experience Health insurance Opportunities for professional development and career growth A safe, collaborative, and supportive work environment How to Apply Send your CV and a cover letter to info@gamico.rw with the subject line "Procurement Officer Application" by 28th October 2026.
