title: Executive Coordinator, ACE-AJ Secretariat
experience_raw: Senior (5+ years of experience)
raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE EXECUTIVE COORDINATOR - ACE-AJ SECRETARIAT Position Executive Coordinator, ACE-AJ Secretariat Host institution Legal Aid Forum (LAF), Rwanda Scope Pan-African / multi-country Reporting ACE-AJ Founding Members, through the governance and hosting arrangements of ACE-AJ and LAF Duty station Kigali,Rwanda,withregularregionaland international engagement Contract Full-time; terms to be specified in the employment contract 1. Institutional Background and Rationale The African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice (ACE-AJ) is a Pan-African platform established to strengthen access to justice, legal empowerment, human rights and people-centred justice across Africa. Its origins lie in a continentally grounded feasibility process undertaken in 2016 through consultations with access-to-justice organisations in Kenya, Sierra Leone, Rwanda, Malawi and South Africa. The feasibility work examined the relevance, scope, sustainability, institutional form and operational requirements of a continental centre and identified the need for a stronger African voice, systematic knowledge exchange, research, learning, capacity development and collaboration among organisations working closest to communities. The feasibility process envisaged the Centre as more than a conventional project or secretariat. It was conceived as a galvanising space for access-to-justice and legal-empowerment actors; a repository of African practice and evidence; a platform for peer learning and exchange; a mechanism for strengthening community-based justice; and a vehicle through which African organisations could develop collective positions and speak with greater coherence on continental and global justice questions. ACE-AJ was officially launched in Kigali, Rwanda, in 2017. Since its establishment, it has evolved into a multi-country network bringing together civil society organisations and justice actors committed to expanding access to justice for poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities. The Legal Aid Forum (LAF), Rwanda, is a founding member and hosts the ACE-AJ Secretariat. ACE-AJ’s Strategic Framework 2024–2030 provides the current institutional roadmap. It organises the Centre’s work around five mutually reinforcing priorities: promoting holistic justice delivery; strengthening capacity building; research and knowledge generation; advocacy and communication; and strengthening the ACE-AJ Secretariat. The Strategy also places substantial emphasis on monitoring, learning, institutional visibility, membership growth, strategic partnerships and diversified resource mobilisation. 2. Purpose and Strategic Character of the Position The Executive Coordinator is the principal executive and operational lead of the ACE-AJ Secretariat. The purpose of the position is to provide disciplined continental coordination and executive leadership for the implementation of ACE-AJ’s Constitution, Strategic Framework 2024–2030, decisions of the General Assembly and Board, approved programmes and institutional commitments. The Executive Coordinator will move ACE-AJ from strategy to implementation. The office holder will connect a geographically dispersed membership, translate strategic priorities into annual and multi-year plans, mobilise resources, coordinate multi-country programmes, strengthen governance and institutional systems, generate and communicate evidence, develop strategic partnerships and position ACE-AJ as a credible African platform on access to justice, legal empowerment and people-centred justice. The position therefore requires a network builder and institutional entrepreneur, not only a programme administrator. The Executive Coordinator must combine continental vision with implementation discipline; diplomacy with accountability; strong member relations with external representation; and programme leadership with fundraising, knowledge generation and organisational development. 3. Overall Accountability Serve as the principal executive focal point for implementation of ACE-AJ’s Strategic Framework 2024–2030 and approved annual priorities. Ensure that decisions of the General Assembly and Board are translated into clear workstreams, responsibilities, timelines, budgets, deliverables and measurable results. Lead the day-to-day work of the Secretariat and coordinate Secretariat personnel, consultants, technical advisers and designated support from member organisations. Maintain effective operational coordination with LAF as host institution while safeguarding ACE-AJ’s distinct continental identity, governance and member ownership. Provide timely, evidence-based advice to the Board on institutional development, programme performance, partnerships, funding, risks and emerging access-to-justice trends. 4. Key Responsibilities 4.1 Continental Network Coordination, Membership and Movement Building Provide proactive day-to-day coordination of ACE-AJ as a Pan-African network and maintain substantive engagement with members across countries, regions, legal traditions and languages. Develop an annual member-engagement architecture covering consultations, focal-person meetings, peer exchanges, communities of practice, thematic working groups, institutional visits and regional or continental convenings. Maintain structured two-way communication between the Secretariat, Board, General Assembly, founding members, and strategic partners. Map and continuously update member expertise, innovations, community-justice models, research, policy experience, institutional capacities and support needs. Strengthen member ownership by creating practical opportunities for members to lead research, training, advocacy, convening and cross-country initiatives. Lead strategic membership growth, with particular attention to geographic balance and stronger representation from underrepresented parts of the continent. Coordinate membership admission, onboarding, orientation, retention and an accurate, functional membership database. Identify common challenges across jurisdictions and convert them into collective learning, research, advocacy and programme initiatives. 4.2 Strategy Implementation and Institutional Performance Translate the 2024–2030 Strategic Framework into costed annual work plans, implementation matrices, institutional calendars and measurable performance commitments. Coordinate implementation across all five strategic priorities and ensure that programme choices remain connected to ACE-AJ’s mission, comparative advantage and member experience. Develop a Secretariat performance dashboard showing progress against strategic outcomes, programme commitments, membership engagement, partnerships, fundraising, visibility and governance decisions. Institute quarterly implementation reviews and prepare concise performance briefs for the Board. Identify implementation bottlenecks, emerging risks and opportunities and recommend corrective measures. Coordinate periodic strategy reviews and contribute evidence for the development of ACE-AJ’s post-2030 strategic direction. 4.3 Holistic and People-Centred Justice Advance ACE-AJ’s agenda on holistic justice delivery by connecting formal, informal and community-based justice actors and approaches. Promote recognition of community-based justice practitioners and strengthen their contribution to accessible, affordable and responsive justice systems. Support member initiatives that demonstrate how legal empowerment, mediation, community justice, legal aid and other people-centred approaches can complement formal justice institutions. Facilitate cross-country learning on enabling policy and regulatory environments for community-based justice and paralegal practice. Ensure that the perspectives of poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities remain central to ACE-AJ’s programmes, research, advocacy and institutional narrative. 4.4 Capacity Building and Peer Learning Develop and coordinate a continental capacity-building programme informed by member needs and the Strategy. Organise practical peer-to-peer learning, mentorship, technical exchanges and cross-country exposure among members. Develop partnerships with universities, legal aid clinics, professional bodies, judiciaries and specialist institutions for training, research and professional development. Promote learning models that draw systematically on the experience of ACE-AJ members rather than relying exclusively on external expertise. Support development of scalable training resources and, where feasible, longer and more intensive learning programmes for community-based justice practitioners. 4.5 Research, Evidence and Knowledge Management Lead implementation of ACE-AJ’s research and knowledge-generation agenda, including practitioner-driven and comparative research with continental policy relevance. Coordinate documentation of best practices, innovations, impact case studies and lessons from member organisations. Develop and maintain an accessible knowledge-sharing platform or e-repository for research, laws, policies, tools, case studies and member resources. Promote common or compatible data-collection approaches across members to strengthen the African evidence base on access to justice. Coordinate research partnerships with universities, research institutions and practitioners and ensure appropriate ethical, data-protection and quality standards. Translate research into policy briefs, position papers, learning products, advocacy messages and practical tools for members and decision-makers. 4.6 Continental Advocacy, Policy Influence and Representation Develop and coordinate ACE-AJ’s continental advocacy agenda, drawing on member evidence and experience. Support development of coherent African positions on legal empowerment, community justice, legal aid, people-centred justice and related emerging issues. Build structured engagement with the African Union, African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights, regional economic communities, United Nations mechanisms and other relevant regional and global institutions. Identify opportunities for ACE-AJ and its members to contribute to justice-sector reform, policy processes, legislative discussions and international forums. Represent ACE-AJ at authorised regional, continental and international engagements and prepare high-quality briefs, statements and speaking points. Ensure that ACE-AJ’s advocacy elevates member expertise and community experience rather than substituting for them. 4.7 Strategic Communication, Visibility and African Narrative Lead implementation of an institutional communication and visibility plan that establishes ACE-AJ as a recognised source of African expertise on access to justice and legal empowerment. Oversee regular member updates, newsletters, website content, social media, publications and other institutional communication. Develop a compelling evidence-based continental narrative demonstrating ACE-AJ’s added value and the contribution of its members. Increase dissemination and citation of ACE-AJ research, policy products and member-generated knowledge. Coordinate media engagement and ensure consistent branding, messaging and recognition of member organisations. 4.8 Resource Mobilisation and Financial Sustainability Develop, maintain and drive a diversified resource-mobilisation strategy and funding pipeline aligned with ACE-AJ’s strategic priorities. Map foundations, bilateral and multilateral partners, international organisations, corporate and philanthropic actors and other potential supporters. Lead or coordinate high-quality concept notes, proposals, budgets, partnership submissions and donor presentations. Build and maintain long-term donor and strategic-partner relationships and coordinate due diligence, negotiations, stewardship and reporting. Explore sustainable non-grant income approaches consistent with ACE-AJ’s mandate, governance and applicable legal requirements. Work with the host institution and relevant governance structures to ensure sound grant management, financial controls, compliance and transparent reporting. Strengthen ACE-AJ’s ability to demonstrate impact as a central element of fundraising and partnership development. 4.9 Programme Development, Multi-country Implementation and Accountability Design and coordinate multi-country and network-wide initiatives from concept development through implementation, monitoring, learning and reporting. Develop clear implementation arrangements with participating members, including roles, deliverables, budgets, timelines, reporting requirements and decision-making arrangements. Track delivery across countries and intervene early where implementation is delayed or quality is at risk. Coordinate narrative and management reporting to the Board, members, partners and donors. Ensure programmes demonstrate clear value to participating members and contribute to ACE-AJ’s strategic outcomes rather than operating as isolated projects. 4.10 Governance and Institutional Development Provide high-quality technical and administrative support to the Board and General Assembly. Coordinate AGMs, Board meetings and other governance processes, including agendas, briefing papers, minutes, decision registers and systematic follow-up. Maintain constitutional, governance, membership, programme and institutional records. Support development, review and implementation of policies, manuals, procedures and internal systems required for a credible continental institution. Ensure Secretariat operations comply with the ACE-AJ Constitution, approved policies, governance decisions and relevant legal and contractual obligations. Support the establishment and effective operation of thematic working groups, committees, patrons or other mechanisms provided for in ACE-AJ’s strategic and governance framework. 5. Expected Results and Performance Indicators ACE-AJ functions as an active, connected and member-owned continental network with demonstrably regular and substantive member participation. Annual strategic priorities and governance decisions are implemented, tracked and reported systematically. Membership expands strategically and becomes more geographically and linguistically representative. Regional and continental exchanges, working groups and joint initiatives produce documented learning and collaborative action. ACE-AJ generates and disseminates credible African evidence, research, best practices and policy products. ACE-AJ’s visibility and participation in relevant African and international justice platforms increases. A credible and diversified funding pipeline is maintained, with stronger donor stewardship and institutional sustainability. Multi-country programmes demonstrate timely delivery, accountability, learning and clear value to participating members. Governance, programme, financial, membership, partnership and communication records are accurate, current and accessible. ACE-AJ increasingly contributes an identifiable African voice to debates and policy processes on access to justice, legal empowerment and people-centred justice. 6. Qualifications and Experience Master’s degree in law, Human Rights, Development Studies, Public Policy, International Relations, Governance, Programme Management or a closely related field. A strong bachelor’s degree combined with substantial relevant senior experience may be considered. At least 5 years of progressively responsible professional experience in access to justice, legal empowerment, human rights, governance, civil society strengthening, international development, network leadership or a closely related field. Demonstrated experience coordinating a network, coalition, secretariat, regional platform or multi-country partnership. Substantial experience working across several African countries is strongly preferred. Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into implementation plans, budgets, partnerships, programmes and measurable results. Strong experience in programme design and management, monitoring and learning, budgeting, reporting and institutional planning. Proven experience in resource mobilisation, proposal development and donor or strategic-partner relationship management. Experience supporting governance bodies and organisational/institutional development. Experience in research, policy engagement, advocacy, knowledge management or capacity development relevant to access to justice is highly desirable. Excellent written and spoken English. Working knowledge of French is a strong advantage; knowledge of other widely used African languages is an asset. 7. Core Competencies and Leadership Profile Continental network leadership and movement building. Strategic execution and disciplined follow-through. Member engagement, coalition management and cross-cultural diplomacy. Resource mobilisation, partnership development and donor stewardship. Programme leadership and multi-country coordination. Governance, institutional development and accountability. Research literacy, evidence use and knowledge translation. High-level writing, communication, advocacy and representation. Sound judgement, political and institutional sensitivity, integrity and independence. Ability to work effectively across borders, time zones, institutions and professional cultures with limited supervision. 8. Particular Profile Sought ACE-AJ is seeking an Executive Coordinator who can build an institution and a continental network at the same time. The successful candidate will be comfortable engaging organisational leaders, practitioners, community-justice actors, academics, donors, governments, regional institutions and international partners. The person must be able to create trust among members while maintaining delivery discipline and accountability. Candidates should demonstrate through concrete examples how they have coordinated networks or multi-country partnerships; converted strategy into implementation; maintained active member participation; handled competing institutional interests; mobilised resources; built strategic partnerships; convened diverse actors; generated or used evidence for policy influence; and contributed to institutional growth, visibility and sustainability. 9. Reporting, Supervision and Working Relationships The Executive Coordinator shall report to the ACE-AJ Founding Members in accordance with the Constitution and shall operate within the agreed hosting arrangements with LAF. The Executive Coordinator will work closely with the Chairperson and other Board members, the General Assembly, member organisations and designated focal persons. For hosted administrative functions, the Executive Coordinator will maintain close operational coordination with the Executive Director and relevant departments of LAF. The Executive Coordinator will supervise ACE-AJ Secretariat personnel and coordinate consultants, technical advisers, interns, service providers and staff designated by member organisations to support ACE-AJ activities, subject to approved structures and budgets. 10. raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE (ToR) FOR THE RECRUITMENT OF THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR Position: Executive DirectorDuty Station: Kigali, Rwanda, Reports to: Chairperson of the Board of DirectorsSupervisory Authority: Board of Directors 1. BACKGROUND AND JUSTIFICATION Association Rwandaise des Conseillers en Traumatisme (ARCT-RUHUKA) is a national non-governmental organisation of professional trauma counsellors established in 1998. The organization evolved from a trauma counselling programme implemented with the support of Trócaire, an Irish charity organisation, in response to the need for trauma counselling and psychosocial support in Rwanda. ARCT-RUHUKA was subsequently formally established and obtained legal recognition as a non-governmental organisation under Ministerial Decree No. 97/11 of 28 July 2007. The organization was later legally registered with the Rwanda Governance Board (RGB) under Legal Personality No. 97/11 dated 12 September 2013. In accordance with the applicable legal and regulatory framework, ARCT-RUHUKA has continued to maintain its legal compliance and institutional standing. Its most recent certificate, issued by the Rwanda Governance Board on 30 September 2026, certifies that Association Rwandaise des Conseillers en Traumatisme (ARCT-RUHUKA), a national non-governmental organization with Legal Personality No. 97/11 of 12 September 2013, complies with Law No. 058/2024 of 20 June 2024 and the related regulations. Over the years, ARCT-RUHUKA has evolved into an established national organisation dedicated to trauma counselling, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), professional capacity development, advocacy, institutional strengthening, and child rights and protection. Through its qualified and committed staff, the organisation works across various sectors and communities in Rwanda, providing technical expertise, professional support, and integrated services that promote mental well-being, strengthen resilience, protect vulnerable populations, and improve the overall well-being of individuals, families, and communities To strengthen its governance, operational efficiency, institutional sustainability, and impact on target populations, ARCT-RUHUKA seeks to recruit a qualified and experienced Executive Director with strong leadership, strategic management, program coordination, resource mobilization, and organizational development skills. The Executive Director will be responsible for the overall day-to-day management of the organization, implementation of decisions made by statutory organs, coordination of staff and programs, development of strategic partnerships, and achievement of institutional objectives in accordance with the organization's mission, vision, statutes, policies, and procedures. 2. OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE POSITION Under the direct supervision of the Chairperson of the Board of Directors and in accordance with the guidance and decisions of the General Assembly and the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will provide strategic leadership and operational management of ARCT-RUHUKA. The Executive Director will ensure effective governance, institutional performance, program quality, resource mobilization, sound human and financial resource management, and the long-term sustainability of the organization. 3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES 3.1. Strategic Leadership and Institutional Governance The Executive Director shall: Provide overall leadership and management to ensure that ARCT-RUHUKA remains an efficient, effective, transparent, and accountable institution; Translate the strategic directions and decisions of the General Assembly and Board of Directors into operational plans and actionable activities; Coordinate the development, review, and implementation of the organization's strategic plan and operational plans, involving all relevant departments and institutional organs; Submit strategic plans, operational plans, budgets, and institutional reports to the Board of Directors for review and approval; Ensure compliance with the organization's statutes, internal regulations, administrative and financial procedures manual, and other institutional policies; Ensure the effective functioning of the organizational structure and propose improvements to strengthen institutional efficiency; Coordinate the preparation of Board of Directors and General Assembly meetings in collaboration with the Chairperson, including agendas, supporting documents, and reports; Ensure timely implementation and follow-up of resolutions, directives, and recommendations from the organization's statutory organs; Propose amendments and improvements to institutional policies, procedures, internal regulations, and other governance documents whenever necessary; Advise the Board of Directors on strategic priorities, institutional risks, development opportunities, and organizational sustainability. 3.2. Administrative and Operational Management The Executive Director shall: Plan, organize, coordinate, supervise, and monitor the day-to-day operations of the Executive Secretariat; Ensure the effective implementation of administrative procedures and internal control systems; Define staff responsibilities and duties in accordance with the approved organizational structure and guidance from the Board of Directors; Ensure effective coordination between departments, decentralized offices, project teams, and operational units; Ensure the availability and efficient utilization of human, material, logistical, and other resources required for the organization's operations; Oversee the management, maintenance, and proper utilization of the organization's assets, infrastructure, equipment, and other property; Strengthen administrative systems, management tools, and internal communication mechanisms; Maintain effective administrative relations with relevant public, private institutions, regulatory authorities, and partners. Identify operational challenges and implement appropriate corrective measures; Ensure business continuity and take immediate action in emergencies within delegated authority, in collaboration with the Board of Directors. 3.3. Program and Project Management The Executive Director shall: Provide overall coordination and supervision of all programs and projects in line with the organization's mission, strategic plan, and contractual obligations; Oversee the development of project proposals, work plans, results frameworks, and budgets in collaboration with program managers and relevant departments; Ensure the technical quality, relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, and sustainability of the organization's interventions; Ensure that programs respond to the needs of beneficiaries and uphold the principles of dignity, confidentiality, safeguarding, and non-discrimination; Coordinate the implementation of training, trauma counselling, clinical supervision, psychosocial support, awareness-raising, and advocacy activities; Ensure that project activities are implemented according to approved timelines, budgets, performance indicators, and expected results; Promote complementarity and synergies among the organization's programs and projects; Organize regular coordination and performance review meetings with staff. Ensure that recommendations from evaluations, audits, monitoring visits, and partner reviews are addressed and implemented; Promote innovation, institutional learning, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement in program quality. 3.4. Financial Management, Budgeting, and Internal Controls In collaboration with the Director of Finance and Administration (DAF), the Executive Director shall: Coordinate the preparation of the organization's consolidated budget and submit it to the Board of Directors for approval; Ensure budget implementation in accordance with approved allocations, donor agreements, and the organization's administrative and financial procedures manual; Regularly monitor budget execution and implement corrective measures to address significant variances; Review and approve financial reports prepared by the Finance and Administration Department before submission to the Board of Directors or partners; Ensure the establishment, maintenance, and effective implementation of internal control systems, risk management mechanisms, and fraud prevention measures; Authorize expenditures, financial commitments, and staff mission orders within the limits of delegated authority; Ensure that financial reports are accurate, reliable, timely, and compliant with statutory, accounting, and donor requirements; Ensure compliance with applicable tax, social security, accounting, and financial regulations; Oversee the preparation and implementation of internal and external audits and ensure timely follow-up of audit recommendations; Promote transparency, accountability, and the efficient utilization of financial and material resources; Ensure compliance with donor-specific financial procedures, grant conditions, and contractual obligations; Support the development of resource diversification and long-term financial sustainability strategies. The Executive Director shall exercise financial authority in accordance with the principles of segregation of duties, dual control, and the organization's approved delegation of authority framework. 3.5. Human Resource Management and Staff Development The Executive Director shall: Implement the organization's human resource management policies in accordance with its statutes, staff regulations, and procedures manual; Identify and plan staffing needs in line with strategic priorities, program requirements, and available resources; Recruit, assign, and supervise permanent and temporary support staff within the limits of delegated authority; Submit proposals for the recruitment of senior management staff and staff termination decisions to the Board of Directors where such decisions fall within its authority; Establish staff performance objectives and conduct regular, transparent, and objective performance appraisals; Promote a professional, inclusive, respectful, and harassment-free working environment; Identify staff capacity-building needs and develop appropriate training and professional development plans; Promote staff motivation, teamwork, accountability, and professional growth; Ensure compliance with applicable labor laws, staff protection policies, and internal procedures; Address workplace conflicts and propose appropriate solutions; Promote succession planning, leadership development, and knowledge transfer within the organization. 3.6. Resource Mobilization, Partnerships, and Institutional Development The Executive Director shall: Develop and submit a resource mobilization and partnership development strategy to the Board of Directors for approval; Identify funding opportunities from bilateral and multilateral donors, United Nations agencies, international NGOs, foundations, and private sector partners; Coordinate the development and submission of project proposals, concept notes, funding applications, and partnership initiatives; Establish, maintain, and strengthen relationships with technical and financial partners, public institutions, civil society organizations, and professional networks; Represent the organization in coordination meetings, forums, platforms, and partnership engagements as delegated; Negotiate partnership opportunities in accordance with the organization's strategic priorities and authorized signing powers; Develop income-generating and self-financing initiatives that are consistent with the organization's mission and statutes; Enhance the visibility, credibility, and institutional positioning of ARCT-RUHUKA; Ensure compliance with funding agreements, contractual commitments, and accountability requirements; Diversify funding sources to reduce dependence on a limited number of donors and strengthen institutional sustainability. 3.7. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning The Executive Director shall: Establish and maintain an integrated system for institutional planning, monitoring, evaluation, reporting, and performance management; Define institutional, programmatic, financial, and administrative performance indicators in collaboration with relevant managers; Supervise the preparation and timely submission of narrative, technical, financial, and institutional reports; Periodically assess progress against operational plans, budgets, and expected results; Organize performance review meetings and ensure follow-up on agreed recommendations; Promote the collection, analysis, and use of reliable data to support evidence-based decision-making; Ensure effective accountability mechanisms for beneficiaries, communities, governance organs, and development partners; Promote knowledge sharing, documentation of good practices, and institutional learning; Oversee the implementation of improvement plans arising from evaluations, audits, and performance reviews. 3.8. Legal Compliance, Ethics, and Risk Management The Executive Director shall: Ensure compliance with the organization's statutes, internal regulations, and applicable laws and regulations governing non-profit organizations in Rwanda; Ensure that the organization meets its legal, administrative, and regulatory obligations to relevant authorities; Coordinate the preparation, maintenance, and updating of legal, administrative, and institutional documents; Ensure the implementation of policies on fraud prevention, anti-corruption, safeguarding, and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse; Identify institutional, financial, operational, legal, and reputational risks and propose appropriate mitigation measures; 0Ensure the protection of personal data, confidentiality of information, and adherence to professional standards in trauma counselling; Coordinate the management of legal matters and disputes in collaboration with the Board of Directors and, where necessary, a legal advisor; Ensure that legal representation and judicial proceedings are conducted in accordance with statutory requirements and the authority delegated by the Board of Directors. 3.9. Institutional Communication and Representation The Executive Director shall: Ensure effective institutional communication within the organization and with external stakeholders; Represent ARCT-RUHUKA in civil, administrative, and partnership matters within the limits of the authority granted; Maintain professional relationships with government authorities, development partners, beneficiaries, and other stakeholders; Oversee the preparation and dissemination of institutional reports, publications, and communication materials; Promote the organization's image, visibility, and reputation in line with its mission, vision, and ethical principles; Submit significant matters requiring strategic decisions or specific representation to the Board of Directors 4. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND PROFILE 4.1. Academic Qualifications The candidate shall: Hold at least a Master's degree or equivalent in Psychology, Clinical Psychology, Mental Health, Psychosocial Support, Social Work, Public Health, Administration, Management, Sociology, Community Development, Development Studies, Project Management, or another relevant field aligned with ARCT-RUHUKA's programmes and strategic objectives. Possess relevant professional experience in trauma counselling, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), child protection, community development, advocacy, institutional capacity building, or the management of non-governmental organisations. Demonstrate proven experience in strategic leadership, organisational management, programme planning, project implementation, resource mobilisation, and donor relations. Have a strong understanding of NGO governance, financial management, human resource management, partnership development, and institutional sustainability. 4.2. Professional Experience The candidate shall demonstrate: At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience in organizational, program, or project management; At least five (5) years of experience in a managerial, leadership, or supervisory position; Practical experience in program coordination, administrative and financial management, strategic planning, and human resource management; Experience managing projects funded by national or international development partners; Experience in the design, development, or implementation of trauma counselling, mental health, or psychosocial support programs shall be a significant advantage; Experience in resource mobilization, partnership development, and institutional management shall be an added advantage. Demonstrate experience working with Community on special attention to vulnerable people , including survivors of trauma, women, children, adolescents, and other at-risk groups. 4.3. Technical Competencies The candidate shall demonstrate: Strong knowledge of strategic and operational planning; Solid skills in program and project management, budgeting, and financial oversight; Good understanding of internal control systems, risk management, and compliance; Strong competencies in human resource management, leadership, and organizational development; Ability to develop funding proposals and negotiate partnerships; Good knowledge of monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning systems; Familiarity with donor requirements and grant management procedures; Knowledge of laws and regulations applicable to non-profit organizations in Rwanda; Proficiency in computer applications and administrative, financial, and reporting systems. 4.4. Language Requirements Excellent command of English and Kinyarwanda, both written and spoken; Good command of French, written and spoken; 4.5. Personal and Behavioral Competencies The candidate shall demonstrate: Strategic leadership and sound decision-making skills; Integrity, honesty, transparency, and high ethical standards; Excellent communication, negotiation, and representation skills; Teamwork and the ability to work in multicultural environments; Strong organizational skills, initiative, and the ability to manage competing priorities; Problem-solving and conflict management abilities; Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines; Sensitivity to mental health, safeguarding, confidentiality, and human dignity; Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of ARCT-RUHUKA. 4.6. Other Requirements Rwandan nationality, if required by the organization's statutes and applicable regulations; Maximum age 45 years, subject to confirmation of compliance with the organization's statutes and applicable laws; Availability for domestic and occasional international travel; A valid Category B driving license shall be an advantage or a requirement if confirmed by the organization's internal regulations. 5. APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS. Interested candidates shall submit an application dossier comprising: A motivation letter addressed to the Chairperson of the Board of Directors of ARCT-RUHUKA; An updated and detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV); Copies of academic qualifications and relevant training certificates; Employment certificates or other evidence of relevant professional experience; Contact details of three professional referees; A copy of a valid national identity card; Criminal records. Any other relevant supporting documents demonstrating the candidate's qualifications and experience. The application submission procedure, receiving address, and deadline shall be communicated in the official vacancy announcement. The recruitment process shall uphold the principles of transparency, fairness, confidentiality, equal opportunity, merit, and prevention of conflicts of interest. 6. Imyanya y’ akazi: # Umwanya (Saba umwe muri iyi myanya ikurikira) 1 Underground Dump Truck Operator 2 Continuous Miner Operator 3 LHD/ Scoop Tram Operator B. Ishami: Ubucukuzi (Mining) C. Atanga raporo kuri: Umugenzuzi w'Ubucukuzi (Mine Supervisor) D. Aho akorera: Trinity Musha Mine / Agace cyangwa ahantu hemewe ho gukorera munsi y'ubutaka E. Intego y'akazi: Gukoresha mu mutekano, neza kandi hakurikijwe amategeko imashini yemewe mu gukata, gukusanya no gusuka amabuye y'agaciro, mu gihe hubahirizwa ingamba z'umutekano zijyanye no guhumeka, kurwanya ivumbi, gukurikirana imyuka, gufata ubutaka, kubuza abantu kwegera imashini, gutandukanya amashanyarazi (isolation) n'aho imashini zihurira n'ubwikorezi. 1. Inshingano: Kwitabira ikiganiro cyo mbere y'akazi (pre-shift briefing) no kwemeza uburyo bwemewe bwo gukata, intera ntarengwa yo kwinjira, uburyo bwo gushyigikira ubutaka, uburyo bwo guhumeka, gahunda yo kurwanya ivumbi, uburyo bwo gutwara amabuye, ibimenyetso by'itumanaho, agace kabuzanyijwe n'inzira yo guhunga. Gukora gusa igihe washyizweho, ufite ubuzima bwiza, wahawe amahugurwa, wasuzumwe mu bikorwa kandi wemerewe gukoresha imashini yihariye (ubwoko n'icyitegererezo), sisitemu ya remote-control n'agace uhabwa gukoreramo munsi y'ubutaka. Kutinjira cyangwa gukata mbere y'uko umugenzuzi w'inzobere atangaza ko aho bakorera hatekanye; kugenzura igisenge, inkuta, aho bacukura, hasi, ibishyigikira ubutaka, amazi, guhumeka, ibikoresho by'ingoboka, kugaragara, ingano y'imyuka n'aho amabuye atwarirwa. Kuzuza no gushyira umukono ku rutonde rw'igenzura mbere yo gutangira rukubiyemo: igice gikata n'ibyuma bikata, boom, umutwe ukusanya, ibipakira, convoyeur (conveyor), umutwe wo gusuka (tailpiece), iminyururu, imiyoboro, insinga, ibirinda, scrubber, ibitera amazi, igikoresho gipima imyuka, impuruza, amatara, ibyuma bihagarika byihutirwa, ibizimya umuriro aho bikenewe, igikoresho kimenya abantu begereye na remote-control. Kudakoresha imashini ifite inenge ikomeye ku mutekano; kuyihagarika, kuyitandukanya n'amashanyarazi, kuyifunga (lock out), kuyishyiraho ikarita y'icyitonderwa (tag) no kuyibuza kugenda, gushyigikira ibice byazamuwe, gutanga raporo y'inenge no gutegereza uruhushya rwanditse rwo kuyikoresha nyuma yo gusanwa no kugeragezwa n'inzobere. Kugerageza no kurinda sisitemu ya remote-control, kwemeza ko imashini ihuye na yo, kugumana igenzura ry'icyuma cyohereza ibimenyetso (transmitter) no gukumira ko imashini yatangira gukora ku buryo butateganyijwe cyangwa butemewe. Gushyiraho no gukurikirana agace kabuzanyijwe ku mpande z'aho imashini ihindukirira, inzira z'iminyururu, ahashobora gufatirwa, imitwe ikata n'ikusanya, convoyeur na tailpiece; guhagarara ako kanya igihe umuntu yinjiye mu gace kabuzanyijwe. Gukorera ku ruhande rwagenewe umutekano ahari ubutaka bushyigikiwe, ureba neza imashini, aho bacukura n'aho amabuye atwarirwa; ntuzahagarare iruhande rw'imashini igenda cyangwa munsi y'igisenge kidashyigikiwe. Kwemeza ko umwuka ukenewe, imyenda ihumeka (curtains), imiyoboro, scrubber n'ibitera amazi biri mu mwanya ukwiye kandi bikora neza; gukora ibipimo by'imyuka bisabwa, ugahagarara, ukazimya imashini ukavamo igihe guhumeka kwanze cyangwa imyuka igeze ku rwego rusaba gufata ingamba. Kudakata hatariho umuvuduko w'amazi ukwiye, ibitera amazi, scrubber n'ibikusanya ivumbi; kugenzura umwuka usubira inyuma no kubuza abantu kwegera ivumbi n'umwuka usubira inyuma. Gutanga impuruza, kugenzura inzira no kugenda buhoro; kurinda insinga, ibigenzura guhumeka, ibishyigikira ubutaka n'abantu, kwita ku hasi habi no guhuza umutwe ukata n'umurongo wo gukata wemewe. Gukata (slumping na shearing) mu byiciro bigenzurwa, mu bujyakuzimu bwa sump, ishusho n'urwego byemewe, mu gihe ukurikirana umutwaro, ihindagurika, ivumbi, imyuka, ibishashi n'ihinduka ry'ubutaka. Gukoresha amaboko akusanya na convoyeur mu buryo bworoshye kugira ngo hatabaho kwifunga cyangwa kunyanyagiza amabuye; ntuzigere ugenzura, ushyiramo ikiganza cyangwa ukuraho ikibuza igihe imashini ifite amashanyarazi; banza wemeze ko nta mbaraga zisigaye mbere yo gukuraho ikibuza. Guhuza gusuka n'imodoka zitwara (shuttle cars), amakamyo cyangwa ubundi bwikorezi ukoresheje ibimenyetso byemewe; kugumana intera, kubuza umuntu kwinjira hagati y'imashini no guhagarara igihe kugaragara, itumanaho cyangwa guhuza bibuze. Kutarenza intera ntarengwa yemewe idashyigikiwe cyangwa ubujyakuzimu bwo gukata; igihe ugeze ku mupaka, uhagarare, umanure ukingire umutwe, uhave, utegereze ko hashyirwaho ibishyigikira kandi ko guhumeka kwiyongera mbere yo gutangira. Gukata ibice bigufi mu butaka bubi, ntuzigere ukora cyangwa unyure munsi y'igisenge kidashyigikiwe, kandi wemeze ko igisenge n'inkuta bitekanye mbere yo gukuramo imashini yapfuye cyangwa gusana. Gukurikirana insinga, moteri, hydraulics n'ubushyuhe buturuka ku guterana; guhagarara iyo hari umwotsi, umuriro, ibishashi, insinga yangiritse cyangwa ubushyuhe bukabije, ukazimya amashanyarazi ugakurikiza gahunda y'ubutabazi bw'ikirombe. Guparika ahantu hagenewe hashyigikiwe, kumanura imitwe ikata n'ikusanya, guhagarika ibikorwa byose, gushyira ibigenzura mu mwanya wa neutral, kuzimya amashanyarazi, gutandukanya aho bikenewe, kurinda transmitter no kuzuza igenzura rikorwa nyuma yo gukoresha. Ntuzigere ucisha ku ruhande ibirinda, interlocks, ibyuma bihagarika byihutirwa, igikoresho kimenya abantu begereye, gupima imyuka cyangwa ibitera amazi; ntuzigere ugendera ku mashini, ukora gusana kutemewe cyangwa ugasiga imashini ifite amashanyarazi nta muntu uyirinze. Kuzuza inyandiko zo gutangira, imyuka, guhumeka, umusaruro, guhindura ibyuma bikata, inenge, gusana, PTO n'ubushobozi, no gutanga raporo ako kanya y'impanuka, ibyenda kuba impanuka n'ibigenzura byananiwe. Kubahiriza Itegeko ry'Ubucukuzi N° 072/2024 ryo mu Rwanda, ibisabwa by'ubuzima n'umutekano mu kazi bireba ubucukuzi, ibisabwa na Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board, amategeko y'ikirombe cya Trinity Musha, uburyo bwemewe bwo guhumeka, gufata ubutaka, gutwara no gutandukanya amashanyarazi, uburyo bwo gukoresha Continuous Miner n'igitabo cy'uwakoze imashini (OEM manual). 2. Ibisabwa ku Kazi, Ubushobozi n'Imyitwarire: Kuba ufite uruhushya rwo gutwara ibinyabiziga rwa category B na F Uburambe bw' imyaka nibura itatu(3) muri uyu mwuga. Icyitonderwa: Usaba ku mwanya wa LHD/ Scoop Tram Operator, agomba kuba azi gukoresha Wheel loader Usaba ku mwanya wa Continuous Miner, agomba kuba azi gukoresha Excavator Kurangiza neza amahugurwa y'ikigo (induction) n'amahugurwa yemewe y'inyigisho n'ay'ibikorwa ya Machine Operator. Isuzuma ry'ubushobozi mu bikorwa no kwemererwa ku mugaragaro gukoresha ubwoko n'icyitegererezo cy'imashini, sisitemu ya remote-control n'agace ahabwa gukoreramo. Icyemezo cy'ubuzima gifite agaciro gikwiriye gukoresha ibikoresho bigendanwa munsi y'ubutaka n'imbaraga z'umubiri uyu murimo usaba. Kugaragaza ubumenyi ku buryo bwo gukata, gahunda zo guhumeka no gufata ubutaka, kurwanya ivumbi, gupima imyuka, gutandukanya no gufunga amashanyarazi, umutekano wa remote-control, uduce tubuzanyijwe, aho imashini zihurira n'ubwikorezi n'uburyo bwo gutabara. Ubushobozi bwo kumenya ibikoresho bifite inenge, ubutaka budashyigikiwe, guhumeka kwanze, imyuka irenze igipimo, ihindagurika ridasanzwe, ubushyuhe bukabije, ibyago by'amashanyarazi n'imikoranire idatekanye y'abantu cyangwa ubwikorezi. Ubushobozi bwo kugumana umwanya utekanye wo gukoreramo, kwita ku kazi igihe kirekire, kugumana remote-control no gutumanaho neza mu gihe cyose cyo gukata. Kuzuza neza inyandiko z'igenzura, umusaruro, imyuka, guhumeka, inenge, gusana n'ubushobozi. Kuza ku kazi neza, gukurikiza amabwiriza mu budahemuka no kwemera gukoresha ububasha bwo guhagarika akazi igihe cyose ikintu gikomeye cy'ingenzi cyabuze. raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE (TOR) Hiring of Logistics Officer October 8th 2026 1. Background Ngali Holdings “The Company” is an investment company located at Kimihurura, Kigali, Rwanda. The organization seeks to recruit a competent and experienced Logistics Officer to lead and oversee Company’s logistics operation. 2. Position Title Logistics Officer 3.Reporting Line Job Details Department People and Culture Job Title Logistics Officer Supervisor HR & Admin Manager Job Purpose: To manage and coordinate the company’s logistics operations, including procurement, transportation, inventory management, and distribution of materials and equipment, ensuring timely, cost-effective, and compliant support for mining operations. Primary Responsibilities Coordinate procurement and delivery of materials, supplies, and equipment. Manage transportation of goods and materials to and from mining sites. Monitor inventory levels and maintain accurate stock records. Ensure timely distribution of materials and supplies to operational units. Liaise with suppliers, transporters, and service providers. Track deliveries and confirm receipt of goods. Ensure compliance with procurement and logistics policies. Prepare logistics and inventory reports for management. Organize storage of equipment and materials in warehouses or depots. Monitor and control logistics costs and optimize resource utilization. Support planning for operational needs and resource allocation. Maintain accurate records of issued and received items. Conduct regular stock counts and reconcile discrepancies. Ensure safe handling, storage, and transport of hazardous materials. Support emergency logistics needs for operations or field projects. Assist in supplier evaluation and selection processes. Coordinate with finance on invoices, payments, and procurement documentation. Maintain updated logistics policies, procedures, and SOPs. Support compliance audits and inspections related to logistics. Recommend improvements to logistics processes and operational efficiency. Use SAP Business One for inventory management, including receipts, issues, transfers, adjustments, reconciliation, and reporting Maintain and regularly update the Company Asset Register. Person specification Academic qualification Bachelor’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or related field. Professional qualification Certifications such as CIPS, CPSM, or equivalent are an advantage. Experience Minimum 3 years of experience in logistics, supply chain, or operational support. Key Performance Indicators Measures Ensure timely, cost-effective, and compliant management of logistics operations, including procurement, transportation, and inventory management. On-time delivery of materials, accurate inventory records, minimized logistics costs, Compliance with procurement policies, and successful support for operational activities without delays or shortages. Accurate inventory records and SAP Business One transactions. Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities: Strong logistics and supply chain management skills. Strong practical knowledge of SAP Business One inventory management. Warehouse, stores, and inventory control skills. Asset management and reconciliation skills. Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Strong judgment, integrity, accountability, and attention to detail. Ability to work under pressure and meet operational deadlines. 4. Application Requirements Interested candidates shall submit: Application letter Updated Curriculum Vitae (CV) Certified academic and professional certificates Copies of identification documents Contacts of at least three professional referees 5. Selection Method Selection shall be conducted through: Shortlisting of qualified candidates Written assessment SAP Business one practical test is mandatory (Candidate who do not attain required pass mark may not proceed to the next stage Interview Reference and background checks 6.
